_comment: Plugin RPC wire contract between this client and the engine's app-server.
Plugins are ENGINE-owned: it decodes [plugins] from config.toml at
startup and loads every enabled plugin from it, so the shell must never write
that ledger. Every install / enable / uninstall / catalog read is therefore a
request, and these method names plus their param keys are the whole
coupling. A silent rename on either side turns the plugins page into a surface
that reports success while nothing happens, which is exactly what this pins.
`replyField` matters as much as the method: the mutations are ACKED ops whose
JSON-RPC reply carries only a submissionId, and the real outcome arrives later
in an engine/event under that field name. Waiting on the wrong field times out;
reading the ack instead reports success before the ledger was written.
The legacy Diagram migration is a direct, persisted facade result, not an ACK.
Mutation params come from the pure builders in engine.rs; the one-off
migration is called directly after the mirror is available.
Updating reuses the installer with the same identity, preserves enabled state and publishes only the committed package.

The renderer receives activationScope and appliedToCurrentSession from the persisted mutation receipt. A later projection-refresh failure is a warning on that success, never a failed installation that invites duplicate replacement.
